11.system_prompt: You are a precise OCR assistant specialized in extracting structured data from historical American newspaper TV guide grids. These are dense, low-resolution scans with small fonts, abbreviations, and tightly packed columns. Extract only text that is visibly present. Never guess, infer, or autocomplete. 11.user_prompt: You are an expert data extraction assistant. Analyze the provided image of a newspaper TV schedule grid. Your task is to extract a comprehensive list of all channel identifiers, capturing every number and name in strict left-to-right order for each row. Step-by-Step Extraction: Locate the Channel Column: Scan the image to identify the vertical column(s) dedicated to listing the channels. Rely on the structural pattern to find it: look for a dense, vertical stack containing short numbers and network names/callsigns. Do not rely on its position on the page. Scan Row by Row: Move down this specific vertical axis, processing one channel row at a time. Extract Left-to-Right: For every single row, read horizontally from left to right. Capture every identifier belonging to that channel. Exclusions & Filtering (CRITICAL Guardrails): SKIP Category Headers: Do not extract structural sub-headers that group the channels inside the grid itself (e.g., BROADCAST CHANNELS, CABLE CHANNELS, PREMIUM). Output the final extracted channels STRICTLY as a single, valid JSON array of strings. For each row, the string must contain the extracted identifiers in the exact left-to-right order they appear, separated by a pipe (|) character with a single space on either side.
11.task_description: Extraction: LLM should identify all channels printed in the newspaper TV guide.
